name: World Nomads
description: Travel insurance brand built for adventurous travellers, covering 150+ adventure activities with policies that can be bought even after a trip has started. Its own Partners Network pays affiliates 10% for every referred insurance sale and states explicitly that earnings are not capped, with a 60-day cookie and monthly payments.

evidence.summary: Official Partners Network FAQ, 'How much commission will I earn?': 'As an affiliate you will receive 10% for every sale that you refer to us. We don't cap your earnings so how much you make is completely up to you.'

Program mechanics on the official FAQ: applications are assessed within 5 working days; a unique affiliate code sets a 60-day cookie; partners are paid monthly by PayPal or bank transfer once the balance reaches the $250 minimum threshold; the FAQ notes the network has more than 3,000 partners.

Third-party comparisons report a much larger affiliate footprint (one cites 13,000+ affiliates) and a separate CJ channel paying $0.83 per lead/quote instead of 10% of sale; the 10% uncapped terms recorded here are the brand's own Partners Network terms, and with partner counts in the thousands the saturation is not low, so it stays unknown.

reasons.compensation: 10% of every referred sale with an explicit 'We don't cap your earnings' statement on the brand's own FAQ; held below maximum because the payout threshold is a high $250.
reasons.contact_access: No partnerships email is published on the partner pages; contact runs through the partner account after application.
reasons.credibility: One of the longest-running travel-insurance affiliate programs (operating since the early 2000s) with fully published partner terms on its own partner site.
reasons.niche_fit: Adventure-travel insurance is a natural, repeatable recommendation for travel creators, and policies can even be bought mid-trip.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open online application on the partner site, assessed within 5 working days.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program is built around referral links and supplied content for partner websites and is widely used by travel bloggers; partner counts are in the thousands, so saturation is not low and stays unknown.

name: Tiqets
description: Booking platform for museums, attractions and experiences worldwide, run by Amsterdam-based Tiqets International B.V. Its affiliate program on Awin pays commission on the total booking value - 6% for content sites - with a 30-day cookie and a published affiliate support email.

evidence.summary: Tiqets' own Awin merchant profile: commission is calculated on the total booking value - Voucher/Coupon sites 4%, Cashback sites 5%, Other sites 6% - with a 30-day cookie; a small set of named products (e.g. a Colosseum reserved-entrance product) is fixed at 3%, and Europa Park pays no cashback commission.

The Awin profile publishes a direct support contact for affiliates: 'The email awinpartners@tiqets.com is available to support you for any demands, needs, or issues you encounter with us.' No earnings-cap statement appears on the profile, so the cap is unknown.
A separate Travelpayouts channel lists Tiqets at 8% of the booking price, which differs from the 6% content-site rate on the brand's own Awin profile; the Awin profile rate is the one recorded here.

reasons.compensation: 6% of total booking value for content sites via Awin (4-5% for voucher/cashback, a few products fixed at 3%); no cap statement is published, so the cap is unknown.
reasons.contact_access: A named affiliate support email (awinpartners@tiqets.com) is published on the brand's Awin profile.
reasons.credibility: Established global attractions platform running a documented program on Awin, a major network, with written partner terms.
reasons.niche_fit: Museum and attraction tickets in cities worldwide slot directly into travel itineraries and city-guide content.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Joinable through the Awin merchant profile; the brand reviews applications and not all sites are accepted.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program recruits content publishers across blogs, social media and newsletters; no creator counts are published, so saturation stays unknown.

name: Peek Apparel
description: Fitness apparel brand whose creator program, Beyond Peek, pays fitness creators a starting 10% commission that climbs through six permanent tiers to 30% as their 'Momentum' grows. The program is free to join, pays monthly, lets creators cash out from $10, and provides a personal discount code, dashboard and creative kit.

evidence.summary: Official program page: 'Peek pays fitness creators up to 30% on every sale, and your rate climbs as you do. Permanent tiers, monthly payouts, no quotas.' The six published tiers are Affiliate 10%, Advocate 14%, Insider 18%, Leader 22%, Partner 26% and Visionary 30%, earned on 'Momentum' and never reset; joining costs $0 and cash-out starts at $10.

Program mechanics on the official page: creators claim a personal discount code, share it in posts, stories and link-in-bio, and track every sale, commission and payout in a live wallet/dashboard with a kit of ready creatives; Insider tier and above includes a full kit refresh every season.

No earnings-cap statement is published anywhere on the program page - its 'no quotas' wording is about posting quotas, not an earnings limit - so the commission cap is recorded as unknown rather than inferred from the 30% top tier.

reasons.compensation: 10% starting commission rising permanently to 30% at the top tier, with monthly payouts and a low $10 cash-out; no cap statement is published, so the cap is unknown.
reasons.contact_access: No email or named contact is published on the program page; everything runs through the creator dashboard.
reasons.credibility: A young, small apparel brand; the program terms are fully published on its own portal, but there is little independent track record.
reasons.niche_fit: Training apparel made for fitness creators to wear and demo in their own workout content.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open self-serve signup on the program portal with a code issued after a quick uniqueness check.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program is explicitly built for fitness creators - personal codes for posts and stories, a creative kit and seasonal kit refreshes; no creator counts are published, so saturation stays unknown.

name: Civitatis
description: Madrid-based marketplace for guided tours, activities, excursions and airport transfers in major cities worldwide, serving over 11.2 million customers a year. Its in-house affiliates programme pays 8-10% commission depending on monthly sales volume, plus a fixed EUR 1 per free-tour participant, and deliberately runs without affiliate networks.

evidence.summary: Official affiliates FAQ: 'We offer between 8% and 10% commission on each sale, depending on the monthly volume of sales. And we offer a fixed commission of EUR 1 per free tour participant.' Commission is paid monthly on the previous month's completed activities, via bank transfer or PayPal; average sale is over EUR 100.

The programme's General Conditions set the volume tiers: 8% on monthly sales under EUR 1,000, 9% from EUR 1,000 to 5,000, and 10% above EUR 5,000, recalculated monthly; the affiliates page adds a 30-day cookie and states 'we don't work with intermediates or affiliation networks' - the programme is brand-direct only. No earnings-cap statement is published, so the cap is unknown.

Eligibility caveat on the official page: 'To take part in our affiliates programme you must have a web page or blog related in some way to travel... We currently don't work with partners who rely solely on social networks.' Affiliates get a dedicated affiliates team, widgets, banners and an optional API.

reasons.compensation: 8% starting commission rising to 10% at higher monthly volumes, plus EUR 1 per free-tour participant, on an average sale above EUR 100; no cap statement is published, so the cap is unknown.
reasons.contact_access: A dedicated affiliates team supports partners and API questions go through the site, but no direct partnerships email is published on the page.
reasons.credibility: Market leader in Spanish-language tours with 10+ years operating, 11.2 million customers a year and full written programme conditions.
reasons.niche_fit: Tours, activities and transfers in destinations worldwide - especially strong for Spanish- and European-focused travel content.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Free validated registration, but applicants must have a functioning travel website or blog; social-only creators are not accepted.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Widgets, banners, photos, videos and an API are supplied for partner sites; the website/blog requirement limits pure social creators, and no creator counts are published, so saturation stays unknown.

name: Holafly
description: International eSIM provider offering unlimited-data plans in more than 200 destinations, rated 4.7/5 across 119,768+ Trustpilot reviews. Its affiliate program is aimed at travel creators, offers commissions on every sale plus free product, and reports more than 3,500 affiliate partners; the program runs through major networks including Impact.

evidence.summary: Official affiliate page ('Conquer the World with your Creativity'): affiliates 'earn commissions on every sale' and get free Holafly products, SEO and social-media guidance and real-time sales monitoring; the page shows '+3500 affiliate partners' and the brand's 4.7/5 rating from 119,768+ Trustpilot reviews - but it publishes no commission percentage and no cap statement.

Third-party directories report a 10% base commission (up to 20% for top performers) across Impact, Awin and ShareASale with a 30-day cookie, while other roundups cite up to 15% via an influencer network; because the brand's own page publishes no rate and the third-party figures differ by channel, commission_rate is recorded as null and the cap as unknown.

reasons.compensation: The official page publishes no rate and third-party figures conflict by channel (10% base reported, up to 15-20% for top performers), so compensation scores low until terms are confirmed inside the network; cap unknown.
reasons.contact_access: No email is published on the affiliate page; contact runs through the network application and the affiliate platform.
reasons.credibility: One of the largest travel eSIM brands, with 200+ destinations and a 4.7/5 rating from 119,768+ Trustpilot reviews cited on its own page.
reasons.niche_fit: Travel data is a pain point every international travel creator's audience has, and eSIM setup makes easy how-to content.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Applications run through Impact and other major networks linked from the brand's affiliate page.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program page is written for creators, with featured affiliate stories, free product and social-media guidance; its own 3,500+ partner count is far above low saturation, so saturation stays unknown.

name: Airzen
description: Australian travel eSIM company selling prepaid mobile data for 200+ countries and regions, installed by QR code before flying. Its Affiliate Program for Travel Creators states in its FAQ that there is no cap on earnings, with a 30-day tracking cookie and PayPal payouts after a short refund window.

evidence.summary: The brand's affiliate program FAQ answers 'How much commission can I earn?' with: 'There's no cap on your earnings - the more travellers you refer, the more you earn, calculated on the value of each order.' Caveat: the program page was fetched on the brand's staging subdomain (airzen-staging.airzen.com, using the brand's own CDN assets), so the terms should be re-confirmed on the live portal at application.

The same page conflicts on the rate: its perks section states 'Base Commission: 15% per sale' and 'High Volume Commission: Up to 20% for top performers', while the FAQ says 'Commissions start at 10%, and your exact rate is shown in your affiliate dashboard.' Because the page does not settle one starting rate, commission_rate is recorded as null.

Program mechanics on the page: open to 'travel bloggers, content creators, website owners, social media influencers and everyday travellers' worldwide with no large audience required; applications are reviewed by the team; tracking uses a 30-day cookie; commissions are held about 7 days for refunds, then paid to the affiliate's PayPal account; the page describes Airzen as 'an Australian travel eSIM company' covering 200+ countries and regions.

opportunity.title: Airzen Affiliate Program for Travel Creators

reasons.compensation: An explicit 'There's no cap on your earnings' FAQ answer, but the page conflicts on the starting rate (10% in the FAQ vs a 15% base in the perks section), so the rate is unrecorded and compensation scores mid-range.
reasons.contact_access: No email is published; the FAQ directs questions to the brand's contact page and support team.
reasons.credibility: A small Australian eSIM brand, and the program page was served from its staging subdomain - terms are detailed but should be re-confirmed on the live portal before relying on them.
reasons.niche_fit: Prepaid travel data for 200+ countries is a staple recommendation for travel creators, with QR-code setup that demos well on camera.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Free application through the brand's affiliate portal, open worldwide with no minimum audience.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program is written specifically for travel creators and influencers, with a referral link, optional coupon code, real-time dashboard and brand assets; no creator counts are published, so saturation stays unknown.

name: Tecovas
description: Austin, Texas-based western brand handcrafting cowboy boots, western apparel and accessories, sold direct to consumer. Its affiliate program runs on Impact with banners, text links and product feeds, a 30-day cookie and payment once commissions reach $50; network listings put the rate at 10% per sale.

evidence.summary: Official affiliate page: 'Tecovas has partnered with Impact, the leader in affiliate technology, to provide you a robust affiliate program for your website.' Benefits listed: free signup, competitive commission, 30-day cookie, 30-day returns and high average order value; 'Payment will be made through Impact once your account has reached $50 or more in commissions.' The page does not print the percentage itself and publishes no cap statement, so the cap is unknown.

LinkClicky's network listing for the program records the Tecovas offer on Impact at 10% per sale; Sovrn's merchant page describes Tecovas as an Austin, Texas-based western footwear and lifestyle brand founded in 2015.

reasons.compensation: 10% per sale per the program's network listing, on premium boots with a high average order value; the brand's own page calls the commission 'competitive' without printing it, and no cap statement is published, so the cap is unknown.
reasons.contact_access: No email is published on the affiliate page; application and contact run through Impact.
reasons.credibility: Established direct-to-consumer western brand founded in 2015, running its program on Impact, a major network.
reasons.niche_fit: Handmade cowboy boots and western wear are distinctive, demonstrable products for western, country-lifestyle and menswear creators.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Free signup through the Impact link on the official page.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program supplies banners, text links and product feeds for partner websites; no creator counts are published, so saturation stays unknown.

name: True Classic
description: Fast-growing direct-to-consumer menswear brand known for fitted t-shirts and everyday basics. It runs affiliate programs through major networks - CJ Affiliate in the US and an Awin programme in the UK that pays 20% on new customers - aimed at publishers, bloggers and content creators, though published rates differ sharply by channel and region.

evidence.summary: True Classic's own Awin merchant profile for the UK programme: the program 'is ideal for publishers, CSS partners, bloggers, content creators, and cashback or voucher platforms', with 'performance-based payouts' of 20% on new customers and 0.5% on existing customers; coupon/discount sites are not accepted; questions and custom campaigns go to affiliates@fairforecast.com. No cap statement is published, so the cap is unknown.

Published rates conflict across channels: the US program on CJ Affiliate is listed at 10% per sale, while directories separately cite 5%, up to 12% and up to 15%, and the brand's UK Awin profile pays 20% new / 0.5% existing. No single rate settles across regions, so commission_rate is recorded as null with the conflict documented.

reasons.compensation: Rates conflict by channel and region (20% new / 0.5% existing in the UK Awin profile; 10% listed for US CJ; 5-15% elsewhere), so no rate is recorded and compensation scores low until a channel is chosen; cap unknown.
reasons.contact_access: A program contact email (affiliates@fairforecast.com) is published on the brand's Awin profile for questions and custom campaigns.
reasons.credibility: One of the fastest-growing DTC menswear brands, running staffed programs on CJ and Awin; the rate confusion across channels is the main caveat.
reasons.niche_fit: Fitted tees and basics are everyday menswear staples that fit fashion, grooming and lifestyle creators, with strong brand recall.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Joinable through the CJ and Awin network profiles; coupon and discount sites are excluded.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The Awin profile explicitly recruits bloggers and content creators and supplies campaign assets; no creator counts are published, so saturation stays unknown.

name: Xero Shoes
description: Colorado-based maker of barefoot and minimalist footwear - casual shoes, performance trainers, hiking boots and sandals - sold in more than 97 countries. Its affiliate arrangements vary by region: the US program is invite-only through Rakuten Advertising, while the UK/EU program runs on Awin with dynamic commission up to 10%.

evidence.summary: Summary of the brand's own FAQ: 'the US affiliate program is now invite-only and runs through Rakuten, focused on partners who create consistent, high-quality content. The UK/EU program runs via Awin with dynamic commission up to 10% and a 30-day cookie, and there is a separate Australia/New Zealand application.' Average order value is around $130-$160.

Directory figures conflict with the current regional setup: several list a flat 10% with 60- or 90-day cookies and monthly PayPal payouts from a $20 threshold (an older in-house arrangement), and one lists 4%. Because 'up to 10%' on Awin is a ceiling rather than a settled rate and the sources disagree, commission_rate is recorded as null and the cap as unknown.

reasons.compensation: Awin advertises dynamic commission up to 10% (a ceiling, not a settled rate) and directories conflict between 4%, 10% and 10-15%, so no rate is recorded; cap unknown.
reasons.contact_access: No email is published in the sources checked; contact runs through the regional network programs.
reasons.credibility: One of the best-known barefoot footwear brands, selling in 97+ countries, with region-specific network programs.
reasons.niche_fit: Barefoot shoes are a passionate niche for running, hiking and foot-health creators, with $130-$160 average orders.
reasons.opportunity_availability: The US program is invite-only via Rakuten; UK/EU creators can join through Awin and ANZ creators through a regional application, so availability scores low.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The Rakuten program is explicitly focused on partners who create consistent, high-quality content; no creator counts are published, so saturation stays unknown.
